metadata.scenario_context: Jeff, Anne, and Sarah are colleagues at a tech startup and have decided to cook together to celebrate some recent achievements they have made within the company. They intend to discuss the recent news reports about AI advancements that could potentially benefit their business.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Peru have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Choosing and discussing the menu for their cooking session.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Jeff, have you ever thought about trying to make a salted caramel dessert? I think it would be a great way to celebrate our recent achievements. 

Also, what do you think about the confidence in the press these days? I feel like Canadians really trust what we read.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jeff
shared_prefix.message: Salted caramel dessert sounds interesting... maybe we could give it a shot. But, um, about the press... I don’t think it’s as reliable as people think. In Peru, we’ve seen a lot of misinformation. I just can't shake the feeling that the press often doesn't tell the full story, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message: I get that... but I really believe that Canadians tend to have a strong confidence in the press. It’s different here. We rely on it for accurate information. But back to the dessert, should we look for a recipe that really highlights that salted aspect? I think we could make it really special.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jeff
shared_prefix.message: Highlighting the salted aspect sounds good... we can definitely find a recipe for that. But, um, I still think trust in the press is overrated. Just because it might be different here doesn’t mean it’s better. I mean, I’ve seen how easily people can be misled. So, what recipe did you have in mind?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message: I understand your concerns, but I really believe that Canadians maintain a lot of confidence in the press overall. It’s just part of our culture. Anyway, for the recipe, I was thinking we could do a salted caramel sauce that we can drizzle over brownies. It would be really delicious! What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jeff
shared_prefix.message: I get what you're saying about Canadians and their confidence in the press... but you know, deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things. Maybe it’s just a difference in experience. But I think we can agree that truth is important, regardless of where we are. Anyway, the salted caramel sauce over brownies sounds amazing! Let’s focus on making that special, yeah?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
